Neither dominant parser has additional sum int64 conversions, round-trip comparisons, safe-integer range guards, or shifted integer-add overflow checks.

The two predicted-name equality loops have 57 source-attributed instructions each in both builds. Cold insertion and remainder inlining/layout also differ. Those differences do not establish the cause of the 24-worker benchmark gap.
The one-worker instrumented captures do not reproduce the observed 24-worker ordering. They cannot establish which startup, compilation, or worker-scheduling behavior accounts for that gap.
conclusion: The available native profiles do not identify another hot safe-integer guard sequence to fix. Do not attribute the multicore gap to a specific mechanism without profiling the 24-worker configurations.
